## Today's Question

How do we repeat one model across groups without turning different contexts
into a misleading ranking?

## Week 14 Plan

- Meeting 1: split, fit, retain, summarize
- Meeting 2: diagnostics and sensitivity by group
- AI model-ranking audit

## Hold The Contract Fixed

- Response and predictors
- Formula
- Units
- Complete-case rule
- Result schema
- Diagnostic rules

## What Changes?

Only the monthly subset changes.

May through September receive the same modeling workflow.

## Checked Modeling Table

```r
model_data <- airquality |>
  transmute(
    observation_id = row_number(),
    month = factor(month.abb[Month], levels = month.abb[5:9]),
    ozone_ppb = Ozone,
    temperature_f = Temp, wind_mph = Wind
  )
```

## Split By Group

```r
month_data <- split(
  model_data,
  model_data$month
)
```

One named data frame per month.

## Reconcile The Split

```r
stopifnot(
  identical(names(month_data), month.abb[5:9]),
  sum(vapply(month_data, nrow, integer(1))) ==
    nrow(model_data)
)
```

## Freeze The Formula

```r
fixed_formula <-
  ozone_ppb ~ temperature_f + wind_mph
```

Do not change group and formula simultaneously.

## One-Group Contract

Require:

- declared columns
- one month
- at least five rows
- predictor variation
- fixed formula

## Return More Than A Number

```r
list(
  month = month_name,
  formula = model_formula,
  fit = fit,
  summary = summary_row
)
```

## Test May First

```r
may_result <- fit_one_month(
  month_data[["May"]],
  "May",
  fixed_formula
)
```

Inspect before automating.

## Repeat The Checked Unit

```r
model_results <- lapply(
  names(month_data),
  function(month_name) {
    fit_one_month(month_data[[month_name]],
                  month_name, fixed_formula)
  }
)
```

## Name The Results

```r
names(model_results) <- names(month_data)
```

Requested group and returned model stay aligned.

## Extract Summary Rows

```r
model_summary <- bind_rows(lapply(
  model_results,
  function(result) result$summary
))
```

## Retain Beside Every Estimate

- group name
- sample size
- coefficient interval
- training RMSE
- training R-squared
- diagnostic evidence

## Check The Batch

```r
stopifnot(
  nrow(model_summary) == 5,
  identical(model_summary$month, names(month_data)),
  sum(model_summary$n_observations) == 116
)
```

## Plot Estimate And Interval

```r
ggplot(model_summary, aes(month, temperature_slope)) +
  geom_errorbar(aes(
    ymin = temperature_low,
    ymax = temperature_high
  )) +
  geom_point()
```

## Why Intervals Matter

Point estimates differ.

Intervals and sample sizes show how uncertain those differences are.

## Different Rows, Different Questions

Each month-specific model describes a different subset.

They are not competitors predicting the same observations.

## Meeting 2 Question

Does automation preserve the evidence that would make one group result fragile?

## One Diagnostic Record Per Group

- standardized-residual flag count
- Cook's-distance flag count
- selected source observation ID
- original coefficient
- sensitivity coefficient
- both training errors

## Preserve Source Identity

```r
removed_index <- which.max(
  abs(rstandard(fit))
)

removed_id <-
  data$observation_id[[removed_index]]
```

## Sensitivity Refit

```r
sensitivity_data <-
  data[-removed_index, , drop = FALSE]

sensitivity_fit <- lm(
  fixed_formula,
  data = sensitivity_data
)
```

## Sensitivity Is A Question

How much does the coefficient change when one declared high-residual row is
removed?

It is not a deletion instruction.

## Classroom Result

Three of five monthly temperature slopes change by more than 40%.

June changes by about 73% and uses only nine observations.

## Why Training Error Falls

The removed row was selected because it was difficult for the original fit.

Lower error on the changed training data is not validation.

## Useful Cross-Group Questions

- Are directions broadly consistent?
- Which intervals are wide?
- Which groups are small?
- Where are diagnostics fragile?
- What context might explain differences?

## Misleading Question

“Which monthly model wins?”

The models do not predict the same observations or answer one competition.

## Generated Ranking

```r
generated_ranking <- model_summary |>
  arrange(desc(r_squared))
```

Sorting is computationally correct; the conclusion may not be.

## AI Claim: September Is Best

Highest monthly training R-squared does not define a common predictive contest.

Different rows and conditions are being modeled.

## AI Claim: Wind Raises June Ozone

- June has nine rows.
- The wind interval includes zero.
- The coefficient is associational.
- The group fit is sensitivity-fragile.

## AI Claim: Ranking Will Persist

All metrics were calculated on training subsets.

No future-observation evidence was used.

## AI Claim: Diagnostics Do Not Matter

Every month has at least one flag.

Three slopes change by over 40% under the declared sensitivity refit.

## Project 2 Transfer

- frozen formula
- one record per requested task
- source identifiers
- declared sensitivity
- training versus validation
- reported instability

## Not A New Project Requirement

The monthly many-model workflow is a teaching example.

Project 2 retains its existing fixed requirements.

## Before Repeating Models

- Fix question and formula.
- Check groups and row counts.
- Test one group.
- Declare output schema.
- Keep failures visible.

## Before Comparing

- Retain sample size and intervals.
- Label training metrics.
- Keep diagnostics and IDs.
- Inspect sensitivity.
- Ask whether rows align.
- State absent new-data evidence.

## Week 15 Boundary

Week 14 builds and audits repeated evidence.

Week 15 communicates the final result clearly and reproducibly.

## Exit Ticket

Name one piece of evidence that prevents a high training R-squared from becoming
an automatic “best model” claim.
